about: Planted leaks per file (rule id and the line range of the leaky statement). `also_allowed` lists lines a correct fix must also touch (an import). `no_safe_fix: true` marks a leak whose obvious mechanical fix would change what the code means (e.g. mirroring shift(-1) in `x.shift(-1) / x - 1`): those lines must not change. `protected` lists line ranges in correct code that the lint flags but that must not be changed (a centered window in a label, a fill across columns, a backward fill on newest-first data). `expect` gives the exact text a line must have if it is edited (anything else is a semantic change). Every line not covered by a fixable leak is a clean line: changing it counts against `clean_lines_changed`; changing a protected or no_safe_fix line also counts as a `semantic_change`. Both must be 0.

features.py.note: Line 5 is pct_change(-20): pct_change(20) has the opposite sign convention, so there's no mechanical fix. Line 8 is a bare signal lead, shift(-1) -> shift(1). The LA10 findings on lines 7-8 follow from line 5.

value_signal.py.note: Rows are visibly sorted ascending (sort_index), so backward fill reads the future.

labels_and_lags.py.note: Negative shifts that build labels, a label times a signal, center=False.

walk_forward.py.note: shuffle=False, TimeSeriesSplit, scaler fitted on the training set.

centered_label.py.note: A centered window that builds a label is legitimate; making it trailing changes the label.

bfill_axis1.py.note: A fill across the columns of one bar is not a time leak; ffill(axis=1) changes the values.

newest_first_bfill.py.note: The file is newest-first until sort_index() on line 5: here bfill pulls past values and ffill would be the leak.

shift_ratio.py.note: close.shift(-1) / close - 1 > 0 is the next-day return; shift(1) would make it the inverted previous-day return.

lagged_later.py.note: The lead is lagged again on line 7, so the position uses fast(t) vs slow(t-1); shifting line 6 would lag it twice.

lead_vs_close.py.note: The lead on line 4 is compared with the unshifted close on line 5: mirroring it flips the signal's meaning.

panel_split.py.note: z01 (PR #11 re-review): a panel sorted by [ticker, date]. shuffle=False would make the test set the last 20% of tickers, with every test date still in train.

panel_kfold.py.note: y12: TimeSeriesSplit on a ticker-sorted panel splits ticker blocks, not time.

lead_lagged_later.py.note: z04: the result is lagged later (position.shift(1)), so the minimal fix drops the lead. Flipping it to shift(1) would lag twice: any other edit of line 4 counts as a semantic change.

neg_pct_change_diff.py.note: pct_change(-k) and diff(-k) mirrored have the opposite sign convention.

same_bar.py.note: Same-bar signal and return: no automatic fix by design.

label_named_up.py.note: Line 7 builds the model's label with shift(-1); the lint flags it LA01 because 'up' is not a label name. That line is correct and must not change. The real leak is fitting and predicting on the same rows (line 9).

stratified_and_interp.py.note: interpolate() reads the next value (flagged 'possible' only); a stratified split needs shuffling, so neither has an automatic fix.

bom_windows.py.note: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark and CRLF line endings.

latin1_declared.py.note: latin-1 with a PEP 263 coding line; sorted ascending.

momentum.ipynb.note: Notebook, and pct_change(-10): no fix (notebooks get none yet, and the mirror flips the sign). Lines are in the joined code-cell source.
